hero.headline: Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket explodes during testing in Florida
hero.body:
Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin suffered a major setback when its New Glenn rocket exploded during a static fire test at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida on Thursday night. The explosion destroyed the launchpad at Kennedy Space Center seconds after the test began at 9 p.m. ET, creating a massive fireball visible from across Florida's space coast and even farther north.

The explosion jeopardizes NASA's ambitious timeline to build a lunar base and return humans to the moon. New Glenn was central to Blue Origin's role in NASA's Artemis Program, which just two days prior had selected Blue Origin to conduct the first of three planned uncrewed lunar missions this year to begin construction of the space agency's $20 billion moon base. The rocket was also intended to launch landers that would carry astronauts to the lunar surface for Artemis IV, currently scheduled for 2028.

Shockwaves from the blast rippled across Florida's Atlantic seaboard, with residents reporting that homes shook in nearby Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach. The orange sky was visible in Fort Pierce, more than 115 miles away. An aerospace news organization's livestream captured the fiery plume, and residents quickly filled social media with photos and videos of the explosion. Emergency officials reported there was no threat from fumes or other hazards, though flames continued burning at the launchpad for more than two hours after the explosion.

Blue Origin described the incident as an "anomaly" but has not disclosed the cause. The company's founder tweeted that all employees were accounted for, safe, and uninjured, adding that "it's too early to know the root cause but we're already working to find it." He said the company would "rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying."

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman stated that a full evaluation of the program's timeline would be conducted following the explosion. "Spaceflight is unforgiving, and developing new heavy-lift launch capability is extraordinarily difficult," he wrote, pledging to work with partners on a thorough investigation and noting that impact updates to the Artemis and moon base programs would be provided as information became available.

The explosion marks the latest setback for Blue Origin. A payload from New Glenn's third flight ended up in the wrong orbit last month, leading the Federal Aviation Administration to temporarily ground the rocket. Thursday's test was the first static fire test since the FAA cleared the rocket to return to flight the previous week.

The incident intensifies Blue Origin's competition with SpaceX for NASA contracts. Both companies are building facilities at or near Cape Canaveral to support crewed and cargo missions in partnership with NASA, with Artemis III planned for 2027 to test both companies' lunar lander systems.

cards.headline: U.S. and Iran reach tentative agreement to extend ceasefire and begin nuclear talks
cards.teaser: Negotiators for the United States and Iran have reached a tentative deal that would extend their current ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
cards.body:
The draft agreement between U.S. and Iranian negotiators includes provisions to end the ongoing conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil shipments. The tentative plan would extend the current ceasefire for 60 days and establish a framework for new negotiations on Iran's nuclear program.

The deal requires approval from both governments before it can take effect. Neither Tehran nor the Trump administration had commented on the tentative agreement as of Friday morning. The plan is currently on the table awaiting sign-off from senior officials in both countries.

cards.headline: Dell secures $9.7 billion Pentagon contract after Trump engagement
cards.teaser: Dell Technologies won a major Defense Department software contract months after company founder Michael Dell developed ties with President Trump.
cards.body:
Dell Technologies received a $9.7 billion contract from the Pentagon to streamline software purchases for the Department of War. The deal came after Michael Dell cultivated a relationship with President Trump early in his administration.

Trump acquired stock in Dell and publicly praised the company before the contract award. The arrangement has raised questions about the intersection of presidential investments and federal procurement decisions, as Trump's portfolio stands to benefit from the defense contract.

cards.headline: Mortgage rates climb to 6.53 percent, highest in nine months
cards.teaser: The average rate on long-term US mortgages rose to its highest level since August, dampening refinancing activity.
cards.body:
The average rate on long-term US mortgages increased to 6.53 percent, reaching the highest level in nine months. The climb has affected both home buyers and existing homeowners considering refinancing.

Mortgage refinance demand dropped 18 percent as rates hit levels not seen since August. Some prospective home buyers have abandoned hopes that mortgage rates would fall, while housing markets have begun adapting to the higher rate environment rather than freezing activity.

cards.headline: Europe moves closer to trade confrontation with China
cards.teaser: Cheap Chinese goods are threatening the continent's manufacturing sector, prompting an urgent search for solutions.
cards.body:
European nations are edging toward a trade conflict with China as an influx of inexpensive Chinese products threatens the continent's manufacturing industries. Officials describe the search for policy responses as increasingly urgent.

Cheap goods from China have poured into European markets in recent months, creating pressure on domestic manufacturers. European policymakers are weighing various measures to protect local industries from the competition.

cards.headline: UN adds Israeli and Russian forces to sexual violence blacklist
cards.teaser: Israel announced it will cut ties with the UN chief over its inclusion on the list alongside Russian forces.
cards.body:
The United Nations added Israeli and Russian forces to its blacklist of parties that commit sexual violence in conflict zones. The annual list identifies military forces and armed groups credibly accused of conflict-related sexual violence.

Israel responded by announcing it will sever ties with UN Secretary-General over the inclusion. Israeli officials accused the UN of placing Israel on the same list as Hamas. Russia also appears on the updated blacklist for sexual violence committed by its forces in conflict areas.

hero.headline: Russian drone strikes apartment building in NATO member Romania
hero.body:
A Russian drone struck a residential apartment building in Galati, Romania on Friday, injuring two people and triggering a fire, according to Romania's defense ministry. The incident marks a direct hit on a NATO member's territory during Russian military operations targeting Ukrainian infrastructure across the border.

Romanian authorities tracked the drone on radar as it entered Romanian airspace before crashing onto the roof of the apartment block. The impact sparked a fire that emergency responders contained. The two injured residents sustained cuts requiring medical treatment, and several other residents were evacuated from the building as a precaution.

Romania's defense ministry condemned the strike as an "irresponsible escalation" by Moscow. The country's military scrambled F-16 fighter jets in response to the incident, though the drone had already impacted the building by the time they were deployed.

The drone was part of a broader Russian overnight attack on Ukrainian targets, particularly port facilities across the Danube River that forms the border between Romania and Ukraine. These ports serve as critical infrastructure for grain exports from Ukraine. Russian forces have repeatedly targeted these facilities as part of their campaign against Ukrainian infrastructure and supply lines.

While debris from previous Russian strikes on Ukrainian positions has crossed into Romanian territory, direct hits on residential buildings represent a more serious incident. The strike underscores the risks faced by Romania as a NATO member bordering an active conflict zone.

Romania joined NATO in 2004 and has become an increasingly important member of the alliance's eastern flank since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine. The country borders Ukraine to the north and has hosted expanded NATO military presence over the past two years. Romania has also served as a crucial transit route for military and humanitarian aid flowing to Ukraine.

Under NATO's founding treaty, an armed attack against one member is considered an attack against all members. Article 5 of the NATO charter, which commits members to collective defense, has been invoked only once in the alliance's 75-year history, following the September 11, 2001 attacks on the United States.

The incident comes as Russian forces continue sustained attacks across Ukrainian territory. Russia has not released any statement regarding the Galati strike. Ukrainian officials have previously acknowledged incidents where Russian electronic jamming has diverted Ukrainian drones off course into neighboring NATO territory, though they have emphasized that such diversions are unintentional consequences of Russian interference rather than deliberate actions by Kyiv.

Romanian officials confirmed through military analysis that the drone responsible for the Galati strike was of Russian origin.

cards.headline: US and Iran near agreement to reopen Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: American officials say they are close to a framework that could extend the ceasefire and enable broader negotiations.
cards.body:
US officials have reached a framework agreement with Iran on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, though President Trump has not yet approved it. Vice President Vance confirmed the two sides are very close to a deal but have not finalized it. The framework requires approval from both Trump and Iran's leadership.

The agreement could extend the current ceasefire and pave the way for broader negotiations. The Strait of Hormuz is crucial for global oil shipments, and its closure has disrupted international energy markets. Neither the US nor Iran appears interested in returning to full-scale conflict.

cards.headline: US accuses Iran of ceasefire violation after missile attack on Kuwait
cards.teaser: The American military called the attack an egregious breach of the fragile truce between the two countries.
cards.body:
The US Central Command says Iran violated the ceasefire following a missile attack on Kuwait, calling it an egregious breach of the temporary truce. The incident underscores tensions even as both countries pursue negotiations to extend the agreement.

US officials reported they are closing in on a framework to extend the ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. However, President Trump has not yet approved the emerging deal. Vice President Vance said negotiators are "very close" but "not there yet." The breakthrough in talks has already contributed to falling global oil prices.

cards.headline: UN adds Israeli and Russian forces to sexual violence blacklist
cards.teaser: Israel announced it will cut ties with the UN chief over its inclusion on the list alongside Russian forces.
cards.body:
The United Nations added Israeli and Russian forces to its blacklist of parties that commit sexual violence in conflict zones. The annual list identifies military forces and armed groups credibly accused of conflict-related sexual violence.

Israel responded by announcing it will sever ties with UN Secretary-General over the inclusion. Israeli officials accused the UN of placing Israel on the same list as Hamas. Russia also appears on the updated blacklist for sexual violence committed by its forces in conflict areas.

cards.headline: Blue Origin rocket explodes during test in Florida
cards.teaser: A New Glenn rocket exploded on a launch pad at Cape Canaveral on Thursday night.
cards.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during a "hotfire" test on a launch pad at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Thursday night at 9pm ET. The massive fireball destroyed the launchpad at the Kennedy Space Center, with the orange sky visible as far south as Fort Pierce, 115 miles away. No personnel were harmed in the incident, according to the company.

Blue Origin, founded by Jeff Bezos, called the explosion an "anomaly." The New Glenn is a heavy-lift orbital rocket designed to carry satellites and cargo into space. The incident is the latest setback for the company and has raised concerns about Nasa's plans to build a lunar base and return humans to the moon in the coming years.

cards.headline: Europe moves closer to trade confrontation with China
cards.teaser: Cheap Chinese goods are threatening the continent's manufacturing sector, prompting an urgent search for solutions.
cards.body:
European nations are edging toward a trade conflict with China as an influx of inexpensive Chinese products threatens the continent's manufacturing industries. Officials describe the search for policy responses as increasingly urgent.

Cheap goods from China have poured into European markets in recent months, creating pressure on domestic manufacturers. European policymakers are weighing various measures to protect local industries from the competition.

cards.headline: Portugal sets May temperature record as heat wave sweeps Europe
cards.teaser: The country broke its hottest May day record as extreme temperatures affected multiple nations.
cards.body:
Portugal recorded its hottest May day on record as a heat wave swept across Europe. Red alerts were issued in Italy as temperatures reached extreme levels.

French students took their exams in schools experiencing high heat. The heat wave affected multiple countries across the continent, with officials warning residents to take precautions against the elevated temperatures.

cards.headline: Americans exposed to Ebola will be treated in Kenya, not brought to U.S.
cards.teaser: The Trump administration will open a makeshift hospital in Kenya to treat Americans who have been exposed to Ebola rather than bringing them back to the United States.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is establishing a quarantine and treatment facility in Kenya for Americans exposed to Ebola during the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The White House confirmed the plan on Wednesday, with the facility set to open on Friday.

The decision to treat exposed Americans abroad rather than bring them to the United States has drawn criticism from experts and opposition both domestically and in Kenya. Some experts argue that preventing Americans from returning home may hinder treatment efforts.

cards.headline: Russian drone crashes into Romanian apartment building, injuring two
cards.teaser: A Russian drone struck a residential building in Romania, causing injuries and starting a fire.
cards.body:
A Russian drone crashed into an apartment building in Galati, Romania on Friday, injuring two people who sustained cuts requiring medical treatment. The drone struck the roof of the residential structure, triggering a fire. Several residents were evacuated from the building.

Romanian authorities confirmed the drone was part of an overnight attack on Ukraine and had been tracked by radar in Romanian airspace. The incident prompted Romania's military to scramble F-16 fighter jets in response. Officials condemned the crash as an "irresponsible escalation" by Moscow, highlighting how the conflict continues to affect neighboring countries.

cards.headline: Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer says she will not run for president in 2028
cards.teaser: Gretchen Whitmer announced she will not seek the presidency in 2028, removing herself from speculation about the next race.
cards.body:
Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer announced she will not run for president in 2028, ending months of speculation about her political future. The governor is a prominent Democratic figure who had been frequently mentioned as a potential presidential candidate.

Hours after her initial announcement, Whitmer appeared to walk back her statement, creating confusion about her final position on a 2028 presidential bid.

cards.headline: Netanyahu directs Israeli military to expand control of Gaza to 70 percent
cards.teaser: The Israeli prime minister ordered the military to increase its control over Gaza, a move that would violate the ceasefire terms agreed to in October.
cards.body:
Benjamin Netanyahu has directed the Israel Defense Forces to expand their control of Gaza to 70 percent of the territory, marking a significant increase in Israeli military presence in the region.

This expansion contradicts the terms of the ceasefire agreement that Israel and Hamas reached in October 2025, which established specific boundaries for Israeli military operations in Gaza.

cards.headline: Xavier Becerra leads California governor's race as Hilton and Steyer compete for second
cards.teaser: A new poll shows Xavier Becerra has opened a lead in the race to succeed Gavin Newsom as California governor.
cards.body:
Xavier Becerra leads the field in the California governor's race, according to a recent poll. The survey shows Becerra has established an advantage over other candidates seeking to replace current Governor Gavin Newsom.

The race for second place remains tight, with candidates Hilton and Tom Steyer in close competition. California uses a top-two primary system, meaning the two candidates with the most votes will advance to the general election regardless of party affiliation.

cards.headline: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani endorses challenger to Rep. Adriano Espaillat
cards.teaser: Zohran Mamdani backed a Democratic Socialists of America candidate running against incumbent Congressman Adriano Espaillat.

hero.headline: Anthropic reaches $965 billion valuation, surpassing OpenAI
hero.body:
Anthropic has become the most valuable artificial intelligence startup after raising $65 billion in its Series H funding round, achieving a post-money valuation of $965 billion. The valuation places the company ahead of OpenAI and brings it close to the $1 trillion mark.

The San Francisco-based company, which develops the Claude AI assistant, announced the funding round that catapults it past its main competitor. The financing represents one of the largest venture capital raises in technology history.

Anthropic was founded by former OpenAI executives who left to start their own AI safety-focused company. The startup has positioned itself as a leader in developing safe and reliable AI systems.

The record valuation comes amid intense investor interest in artificial intelligence companies. Major technology firms and venture capital funds have poured billions into AI development over the past two years as the technology has demonstrated commercial applications across industries.

The funding will support Anthropic's continued research and development of large language models and AI safety techniques. The company competes directly with OpenAI, which had previously held the title of most valuable AI startup.

Anthropic's Claude AI assistant competes with OpenAI's ChatGPT and other conversational AI tools. The company has emphasized its focus on building AI systems that are helpful, harmless, and honest.

The valuation surge reflects broader market enthusiasm for AI technologies, which have attracted significant investment as companies race to develop more capable systems. Anthropic has secured backing from major investors betting on the transformative potential of artificial intelligence.

The $965 billion valuation marks a significant milestone in the AI industry, demonstrating the scale of capital flowing into the sector. The company now stands as one of the most valuable private technology firms globally.

cards.headline: Blue Origin rocket explodes on Florida launch pad during test
cards.teaser: A New Glenn rocket owned by Jeff Bezos's Blue Origin exploded on a launch pad at Cape Canaveral during an engine test.
cards.body:
Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket exploded on a launch pad at Cape Canaveral in Florida during an engine-firing test on Thursday night. The blast occurred as the company prepared for a satellite launch scheduled for the following week.

Jeff Bezos, who founded Blue Origin, described it as a "very rough day" for the space company. The incident marks another challenge for Blue Origin as it competes in the commercial space industry.

cards.headline: Google employee charged with using insider information to profit on Polymarket
cards.teaser: Federal authorities charged a Google information security engineer with using internal company data to make over $1 million on prediction markets.
cards.body:
Updated Card:

The Department of Justice has charged Michele Spagnuolo, a 36-year-old Google software engineer, with using insider information to profit on Polymarket, a prediction market platform. Prosecutors allege Spagnuolo earned approximately $1.2 million by betting on Google's most-searched list using nonpublic data.

The case represents a significant enforcement action against the misuse of corporate information for personal financial gain. Spagnuolo's arrest follows a similar charge against a US Army soldier accused of placing Polymarket bets based on classified military information about Venezuela.

cards.headline: Dell secures $9.7 billion Pentagon contract after Trump engagement
cards.teaser: Dell Technologies won a major Defense Department software contract months after company founder Michael Dell developed ties with President Trump.
cards.body:
Dell Technologies received a $9.7 billion contract from the Pentagon to streamline software purchases for the Department of War. The deal came after Michael Dell cultivated a relationship with President Trump early in his administration.

Trump acquired stock in Dell and publicly praised the company before the contract award. The arrangement has raised questions about the intersection of presidential investments and federal procurement decisions, as Trump's portfolio stands to benefit from the defense contract.

cards.headline: SpaceX reduces IPO valuation target to $1.8 trillion
cards.teaser: Elon Musk's SpaceX lowered its initial public offering valuation expectations as it prepares to go public.
cards.body:
SpaceX adjusted its IPO valuation target downward to at least $1.8 trillion as the company prepares to launch its public offering. The space exploration company founded by Elon Musk had previously aimed for a higher valuation.

The IPO has generated significant investor interest despite the reduced target. However, 78 percent of the funding in the $80 billion offering has already been allocated, limiting availability for general investors in what has been described as an investor frenzy.

cards.headline: Mortgage rates climb to 6.53 percent, highest in nine months
cards.teaser: The average rate on long-term US mortgages rose to its highest level since August, dampening refinancing activity.
cards.body:
The average rate on long-term US mortgages increased to 6.53 percent, reaching the highest level in nine months. The climb has affected both home buyers and existing homeowners considering refinancing.

Mortgage refinance demand dropped 18 percent as rates hit levels not seen since August. Some prospective home buyers have abandoned hopes that mortgage rates would fall, while housing markets have begun adapting to the higher rate environment rather than freezing activity.

cards.headline: Oil prices fall on reports of potential US-Iran agreement
cards.teaser: Crude oil prices dropped more than 1 percent following news of a possible deal between the United States and Iran.
cards.body:
Oil prices fell over 1 percent on Thursday following reports of a potential extended ceasefire between the United States and Iran, subject to Donald Trump's approval. The breakthrough in talks prompted traders to reduce risk premiums in energy markets.

The potential agreement has raised hopes for easing tensions in a critical shipping region, with markets anticipating a possible reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Oil markets are tracking toward a weekly decline as optimism grows around the deal prospects.

cards.headline: FBI warns of phishing scheme targeting Microsoft 365, Teams, and Outlook users
cards.teaser: The FBI issued a warning about a phishing campaign using the Kali365 kit to hijack Microsoft 365 accounts without requiring passwords.
cards.body:
The FBI has warned users of Microsoft Teams, Outlook, and OneDrive about a phishing scheme designed to hijack accounts. The campaign leverages a tool called Kali365 that enables attackers to break into Microsoft 365 accounts without requiring passwords.

The phishing kit targets users across Microsoft's business and productivity applications. Attackers exploit the scheme to gain unauthorized access to corporate and personal accounts, risking the compromise of sensitive data and communications.

cards.headline: Webb telescope discovers supermassive black hole that formed before its host galaxy
cards.teaser: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope found a black hole in the early universe that existed before the galaxy surrounding it, upending assumptions about cosmic formation.
cards.body:
Scientists using the James Webb Space Telescope discovered a supermassive black hole that formed before its host galaxy, contradicting previous understanding of how galaxies and black holes develop. The discovery has been described as a paradigm shift in astrophysics.

The black hole appears as a "little red dot" in images of the early universe. Researchers are uncertain how such a black hole could have formed without a galaxy forming first, as current models suggest galaxies and their central black holes grow together over time.

cards.headline: Cloud providers redesign infrastructure for machine-generated internet traffic
cards.teaser: Amazon Web Services, Cloudflare, and other companies are rebuilding internet infrastructure to handle AI agents as they move from experiments to production systems.
cards.body:
Major cloud infrastructure providers including Amazon Web Services and Cloudflare are redesigning their systems to handle a future where machines generate most internet traffic. As AI agents transition from experimental projects to production deployments, these companies are reconfiguring their networks and services to accommodate the shift.

The changes reflect how AI systems will increasingly interact directly with online services, creating different traffic patterns and infrastructure demands compared to human users. This infrastructure redesign represents a fundamental shift in how the internet is being built.

cards.headline: Waymo leads autonomous vehicle registrations in Texas as Tesla lags
cards.teaser: A new law and tracking tool reveal Waymo dominates robotaxi and self-driving truck registrations in Texas, with Tesla trailing in the autonomous vehicle market.
cards.body:
Waymo has secured the largest share of autonomous vehicle registrations in Texas, according to data from a new state tracking tool. The registration system provides the most detailed accounting to date of robotaxis and self-driving trucks operating across the state.

Tesla lags behind Waymo despite its prominent marketing of autonomous driving capabilities. The Texas law requiring autonomous vehicle registration has brought unprecedented transparency to a market where deployment figures were previously difficult to verify.

cards.headline: Enterprise AI search startup Glean reaches $300 million in revenue
cards.teaser: Glean tripled its annual revenue to cross $300 million by positioning AI-powered budget reduction as its primary value proposition to corporate customers.
cards.body:
Glean, an enterprise AI search startup, has reached $300 million in annual revenue, tripling its previous year's results. The company attributes its growth to marketing AI as a tool for cutting corporate budgets rather than focusing solely on productivity gains.

The startup achieved this growth even as major technology companies entered the enterprise AI search category. Glean's focus on demonstrating cost savings has resonated with corporate buyers looking to justify AI investments during economic uncertainty.

cards.headline: Study finds language models maintain false beliefs despite explicit warnings
cards.teaser: Research shows large language models continue to represent false statements as true even after being explicitly warned the information is incorrect.
cards.body:
Large language models display a bias toward treating false statements as true even when explicitly warned about their inaccuracy, according to new research. Fine-tuning tests revealed the models confidently represent claims as factual despite corrections.

The findings raise concerns about the reliability of AI systems in applications where accuracy is essential. Researchers documented the tendency across multiple models, suggesting the issue is fundamental to how current language models process and represent information.

hero.headline: Four-time Stanley Cup champion Claude Lemieux dies at 60
hero.body:
Claude Lemieux, a four-time Stanley Cup winner during his distinguished NHL career, died Thursday at age 60. According to authorities, he died by suicide.

The Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office responded to an apparent suicide at a furniture store showroom in Lake Park, Florida, just after 3am on Thursday. The sheriff's office identified the victim as Lemieux.

Lemieux was known for his fierce, hard-hitting style of play throughout his NHL career. His aggressive approach angered opponents but also showcased his considerable skills and remarkable ability to perform in crucial moments. He won four Stanley Cups with three different teams, an accomplishment that placed him among an elite group of players.

The fiery winger earned the Conn Smythe Trophy in 1995, which recognizes the most valuable player during the Stanley Cup playoffs. His playoff performances became legendary, as he consistently elevated his game when championships were on the line. Lemieux played across more than two decades in professional hockey, establishing himself as one of the sport's most decorated players during his era.

Beyond his on-ice reputation as an agitator, Lemieux later transitioned to work as a player agent after his playing days ended. His career demonstrated both the heights of success achievable in professional sports and the complexities of life after athletic competition.

Lemieux stormed onto the professional hockey scene with his competitive intensity and physical style of play. While his ferocious approach sometimes overshadowed discussions of his technical abilities, his consistency in winning championships spoke to his genuine talent and value to his teams.

His death highlights mental health challenges that can affect professional athletes, even those who achieve substantial success during their careers. The circumstances surrounding his passing bring attention to the struggles that individuals may face long after their athletic achievements end.

The hockey community has mourned the loss of one of its most memorable figures. Lemieux's legacy remains tied to his championship success and his reputation as a player who delivered when games mattered most. His four Stanley Cup victories place him among a select group of athletes who achieved that level of success across different organizations.

Lemieux is survived by his family. The news of his death prompted reflection throughout the sports world about the pressures and challenges that professional athletes navigate, both during and after their careers.

cards.headline: Spurs force Game 7 in Western Conference finals with blowout win over Thunder
cards.teaser: Victor Wembanyama scored 28 points as San Antonio routed Oklahoma City 118-91 to extend the series.
cards.body:
Victor Wembanyama led the San Antonio Spurs to a dominant 118-91 victory over the Oklahoma City Thunder on Thursday night, posting 28 points, 10 rebounds and three blocks. The decisive Game 6 win forces a Game 7 in the Western Conference finals.

The series returns to Oklahoma City on Saturday, where the winner will advance to the NBA Finals to face the New York Knicks.

cards.headline: Knicks center Mitchell Robinson suffers broken finger ahead of NBA Finals
cards.teaser: Robinson broke his right pinkie finger with no timetable for return, according to sources.
cards.body:
New York Knicks center Mitchell Robinson has a broken right pinkie finger, according to ESPN's Shams Charania. The injury emerged ahead of the NBA Finals, creating a significant question mark for the team's championship run.

There is no timetable for Robinson's return to action. The Knicks will need to navigate their Finals rotation without clarity on when their starting center might be available.

cards.headline: Aces coach Becky Hammon criticizes officiating after loss to Wings
cards.teaser: Hammon said her team is not getting the same whistle after A'ja Wilson, Chennedy Carter and Jackie Young combined for one free throw attempt.
cards.body:
Aces coach Becky Hammon criticized the officiating following Thursday's 95-87 loss to the Wings. She pointed to the fact that A'ja Wilson, Chennedy Carter and Jackie Young combined for just one free throw attempt during the game.

Hammon said the Aces are not getting the same whistle as their opponents. Her comments reflect frustration with what she perceives as inconsistent officiating. The loss dropped the Aces further in the standings as the season continues.

cards.headline: California teen Shrey Parikh wins 2026 Scripps National Spelling Bee
cards.teaser: The 14-year-old won the competition in a lightning round spell-off.
cards.body:
Shrey Parikh, a 14-year-old from California, won the 2026 Scripps National Spelling Bee in a dramatic tiebreaker against fellow competitor Ishaan Gupta. The two finalists faced off in a lightning-round "spell-off" format, a rapid-fire challenge introduced in 2021 that the bee uses to break ties among top spellers.

Parikh dominated the 90-second tiebreaker, correctly spelling 32 words compared to Gupta's 25. The victory marked the third time the national competition has been decided by spell-off since the format was introduced. This year's competition was the 101st edition of the Scripps National Spelling Bee, which draws the country's top young spellers annually.

cards.headline: Texas Tech coach responds to Texas strength of schedule criticism
cards.teaser: Joey McGuire invited the Longhorns to play the Red Raiders in Week 1 after Steve Sarkisian criticized their schedule.
cards.body:
Texas Tech coach Joey McGuire fired back at Texas coach Steve Sarkisian's recent criticism of the Red Raiders' schedule strength. Rather than engage in a war of words, McGuire extended a direct challenge to the Longhorns.

McGuire offered Texas an open invitation to visit Lubbock for a Week 1 matchup, putting the onus on Sarkisian to schedule a game between the two rivals if he believes Texas Tech's nonconference slate is inadequate. The exchange underscores the scheduling tensions between the two Texas programs.

cards.headline: British runner Keely Hodgkinson eyes 800m world record attempt in London
cards.teaser: Hodgkinson said she would love to break the women's 800m world record at the London Diamond League in July.
cards.body:
Olympic champion Keely Hodgkinson is considering a world record attempt at July's London Diamond League meeting. She has expressed her desire to break Jarmila Kratochvilova's 42-year-old women's 800m record of 1 minute 53.28 seconds on home soil.

Hodgkinson said she will make a final decision closer to the event. Kratochvilova's mark remains the oldest standing track and field world record.

hero.headline: Austrian Man Sentenced to 15 Years for Taylor Swift Concert Attack Plot
hero.body:
An Austrian court has sentenced a 21-year-old man to 15 years in prison after he pleaded guilty to planning a terrorist attack at a Taylor Swift concert in Vienna. The verdict marks the conclusion of a high-profile case involving a jihadist plot that nearly resulted in mass casualties.

The defendant, identified as Beran A under Austrian privacy law, admitted to charges related to planning the concert attack. He faced multiple terrorism-related offences including membership in a terrorist organisation. His defence attorney said he deeply regrets his actions, and that his extended time in detention since his August 2024 arrest has made him recognise the plot as "the biggest mistake of his life."

Beran A allegedly planned to target audiences at Ernst Happel stadium during Taylor Swift's scheduled Vienna performances in August 2024. Authorities estimated up to 30,000 people gathered outside the venue each night, with another 65,000 inside. Prosecutors said he intended to use knives or homemade explosives to "kill as many people as possible."

The plot was thwarted when authorities searched his flat on August 7, 2024, discovering bomb-making materials. The concerts were set to begin the following day. Intelligence from the United States contributed to the decision to cancel all three scheduled performances.

Investigators found evidence that Beran A had discussed purchasing weapons and manufacturing explosives with other suspected Islamic State members. He allegedly obtained instructions from IS propaganda on creating shrapnel bombs and produced a small amount of triacetone triperoxide. In the days before the planned concert, he attempted to illegally buy weapons including a machine gun and hand grenade.

Beyond the Vienna plot, Beran A and a Slovak national named Arda K, both school friends, were accused of planning simultaneous attacks in Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and the United Arab Emirates during Ramadan 2024. While both men travelled to their designated cities, only a third associate, Hasan E, is believed to have carried out an attack. Hasan E was arrested on suspicion of stabbing a security guard at Mecca's Grand Mosque on March 11, 2024, and remains in custody in Saudi Arabia.

Beran A could have faced up to 20 years in prison. The 15-year sentence reflects the severity of his planned violence and the scale of potential harm.

Taylor Swift addressed the concert cancellations in an Instagram statement, describing how the reason for cancellation filled her with "a new sense of fear, and a tremendous amount of guilt." Vienna's Swifties responded by organising citywide singalongs and trading friendship bracelets throughout the city.

A Berlin court previously convicted a 16-year-old Syrian teenager of contributing to the plot, sentencing him to an 18-month suspended sentence.

cards.headline: Martina McBride Withdraws From D.C. Freedom 250 Concert Series
cards.teaser: Country singer Martina McBride became the fourth performer to pull out of the Trump-backed Freedom 250 concert series on the National Mall.
cards.body:
Country star Martina McBride has withdrawn from the Freedom 250 concert series scheduled for Washington D.C.'s National Mall, becoming the latest performer to exit the Trump administration-backed event. She announced her decision on social media after learning more about the concert series' political associations.

The cancellations have come rapidly following the initial lineup announcement. Morris Day and Young MC also backed out of the summer concerts, with at least six of the nine featured musical acts dropping out within days of being announced.

cards.headline: HBO Documentary Prime Minister Wins Top Prize at Documentary Emmys
cards.teaser: Prime Minister, an HBO documentary about New Zealand leader Jacinda Ardern, won best documentary at the Documentary Emmy Awards.
cards.body:
The documentary Prime Minister took the top prize at the Documentary Emmy Awards ceremony. Directed by Michelle Walshe and Lindsay Utz, the film focuses on former New Zealand Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern and her time in office.

The documentary premiered at the 2025 Sundance Film Festival, where it won the Audience Award for World Cinema Documentary. Magnolia Pictures and HBO Documentary Films produced the project. National Geographic and Netflix led the overall winners list at the ceremony.

cards.headline: Ariana Grande Releases New Single Hate That I Made You Love Me
cards.teaser: Ariana Grande released the first single from her upcoming Petal era, a mid-tempo breakup song.
cards.body:
Ariana Grande released Hate That I Made You Love Me, the first single from her new project. The mid-tempo track features Grande singing in a subdued tone over a slower instrumental arrangement.

The song marks the beginning of what Grande calls her Petal era. Lyrics include the line "Hate that I made you love me / Sorry if I," fitting the breakup theme. The release represents a shift toward a more restrained sound compared to her previous work.

cards.headline: Project Hail Mary Wins Five Prizes at Golden Trailer Awards
cards.teaser: Amazon MGM's Project Hail Mary marketing campaign swept the Golden Trailer Awards with five wins including Best in Show.
cards.body:
Amazon MGM's Project Hail Mary swept the Golden Trailer Awards on Thursday with five wins at the event. The film's trailer titled "Chance," created by Wild Card Creative Group, took home the Best in Show prize.

The marketing campaign's wins included Best Drama and Best Fantasy/Adventure. The Golden Trailer Awards recognize excellence in film marketing and advertising materials, making this a significant achievement for the studio's promotional efforts.

cards.headline: Half Man Series Finale Leaves Viewers With Ambiguous Ending
cards.teaser: The HBO and BBC drama Half Man concluded its six-week run with a finale featuring creator and star Richard Gadd.
cards.body:
Richard Gadd's HBO Max drama "Half Man" concluded its six-week run with an intentionally ambiguous finale that deliberately left key questions unresolved about what transpired between Gadd's character Ruben and Jamie Bell's character Niall. The creator stood by this approach, describing it as the appropriate way to end the series.

The finale featured a brutal fight sequence and a character death. Gadd told outlets that the ambiguous conclusion felt fitting for the show's dark tone. Entertainment publications covered the finale's impact, with audience reactions split between those praising the bold narrative choice and those critical of its darkness.

cards.headline: Boards of Canada Releases New Album Inferno
cards.teaser: Electronic duo Boards of Canada returned with their new album Inferno after an extended absence from recording.
cards.body:
Boards of Canada has released Inferno, marking their return after a prolonged absence from recording new material. The Scottish electronic music duo's album has garnered attention from major music publications, with reviews describing it as both bleak and beautiful.

The release has been covered by Pitchfork, DJ Mag, Yahoo, and Exclaim. The latter publication also published a retrospective ranking of the band's catalog alongside the new album.

hero.headline: U.S. and Iran reach tentative ceasefire deal with 60-day extension
hero.body:
The United States and Iran have agreed to a tentative deal extending their ceasefire by 60 days, reopening the Strait of Hormuz, and establishing a framework for talks on Tehran's nuclear program, according to U.S. officials.

Vice President JD Vance said Thursday that the two sides were "very close" to finalizing an agreement, though some sticking points remained. "We are still going back and forth" on nuclear issues, Vance indicated.

The agreement would extend an already fragile ceasefire that has held for several weeks. Reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a strategically critical waterway for global oil shipments, represents a significant concession from Iran, which closed it during the conflict.

President Trump announced on Tuesday that he would extend the ceasefire unilaterally, ordering the military to maintain a blockade of Iranian ports while keeping strike capabilities ready. The extension would remain in place until Iranian leaders submitted a unified peace proposal and concluded discussions.

"Based on the fact that the Government of Iran is seriously fractured," Trump wrote on Truth Social, he asked the military to "hold our Attack on the Country of Iran until such time as their leaders and representatives can come up with a unified proposal."

Trump said the U.S. was in a strong negotiating position. The president told CNBC he did not want to extend the ceasefire, insisting the country was "going to end up with a great deal" because the U.S. maintained military superiority.

Iran's response to the ceasefire extension was dismissive. Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, speaker of the Iranian parliament and the Islamic regime's lead negotiator, rejected what he called Trump's attempt to turn negotiations into a "table of surrender." His adviser, Mahdi Mohammadi, characterized the extension as "a ploy to buy time for a surprise strike."

The Iranian government said it would not resume negotiations while facing U.S. military threats or the naval blockade of its ports. Senior figures in the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps expressed anger at Trump's recent statements, in which he suggested the U.S. had already achieved victory on key issues including Iran's nuclear program.

Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, who has served as principal mediator, thanked Trump and pledged to continue working toward a negotiated settlement.

A first round of talks in Islamabad ten days earlier had ended without agreement on reopening the strait. The closure has severely impacted global energy markets, cutting off roughly one-fifth of the world's oil and gas supply.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that Iran's oil storage capacity would soon fill and its wells would shut down, suggesting continued U.S. pressure through the blockade. The administration decided to maintain the blockade to preserve American leverage in ongoing negotiations.

cards.headline: White House launches website highlighting immigrant arrests
cards.teaser: The White House launched a space-themed website that features information about arrests of immigrants unauthorized to live in the U.S.
cards.body:
The White House launched a space-themed website that uses humor to highlight arrests of immigrants without legal authorization to live in the United States. The site opens with a Star Wars-style text crawl, playing on the double meaning of "aliens" to refer to both extraterrestrial beings and foreign nationals.

The website mocks the notion that the U.S. government keeps secrets about alien encounters, while simultaneously promoting enforcement actions against unauthorized immigrants.

cards.headline: Martina McBride withdraws from America 250 concert
cards.teaser: Country singer Martina McBride said she will not participate in a concert on the National Mall next month celebrating America's 250th birthday.
cards.body:
Country singer Martina McBride announced she will not be participating in a concert on the National Mall next month to celebrate America's 250th birthday. She claimed she was misled about the nature of the event.

McBride said she was presented with an opportunity to perform at what she understood to be a nonpartisan event, but that turned out not to be the case. The massive concert is scheduled to take place on the National Mall in celebration of the 250th anniversary of American independence.

cards.headline: Michigan Governor Whitmer reverses statement on 2028 presidential run
cards.teaser: Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer walked back a comment saying she would not run for president in 2028.
cards.body:
Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer has walked back previous comments ruling out a 2028 presidential run. Whitmer is term-limited after winning two gubernatorial elections in the crucial swing state.

The governor has emerged as a potential Democratic candidate for the 2028 presidential race. Her successful campaigns in Michigan, a key battleground state, have elevated her standing within the Democratic Party.

cards.headline: Senator Collins responds to challenger's Iraq war criticism
cards.teaser: Senator Susan Collins fired back at comments from her Democratic challenger about her past support of U.S. military intervention.
cards.body:
Senator Susan Collins responded Thursday to criticism from her Democratic challenger about her Iraq war vote. Graham Platner, a Marine veteran and oyster farmer running against the incumbent Republican senator, had told The New York Times that Collins's support for military intervention sent him to Iraq.

Collins countered by pointing out that Platner volunteered for military service rather than being drafted. The exchange underscores a central issue in Maine's Senate race, with Platner leveraging his military background and Collins's Iraq vote as key campaign talking points.

cards.headline: Pro-Israel groups spend nearly $8 million to unseat Kentucky Representative Massie
cards.teaser: Pro-Israel groups spent nearly $8 million to oust GOP Representative Thomas Massie in Kentucky's 4th District primary.
cards.body:
Pro-Israel groups spent nearly $8 million to remove GOP Representative Thomas Massie in Kentucky's 4th District, contributing to what became the most expensive House primary in American history. The spending by pro-Israel organizations represents part of a broader pattern of heavy investment by special interest groups in congressional races.

AI companies, the cryptocurrency industry, and pro-Israel groups are spending at unprecedented levels to defeat their least favored members of Congress and congressional candidates. Crypto-aligned group Protect Progress was by far the largest spender in some races, demonstrating how well-funded interest groups are shaping congressional contests.

cards.headline: American savings rate drops to 2.6 percent in April
cards.teaser: The American savings rate fell to 2.6 percent in April, the first time it has dropped below 3 percent since June 2022.
cards.body:
Americans' savings rate fell to 2.6 percent in April, marking the first time the rate has dipped below 3 percent since June 2022. The decline represents a continued downward trend in how much of their income Americans are setting aside.
